rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding command implies taking abundant provisions together with piety; because people are deficient, accumulating provisions tends toward tyranny, except for the few God protects.
rows.anchor: فأكثروا من الزاد مصحوبا بالتقوى وكان الإنسان محل النقصان فكان الإكثار حاملا له في العادة على الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God attaches the command to fear Him to Himself to emphasize sincere devotion for His own sake, rather than hope, fear, or a status associated with pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: مؤكدا لأمر التقوى مشرفا لها بالإضافة إلى نفسه الشريفة تنبيها على الإخلاص لأجل ذاته السنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of sound understanding are those whose clear intellects have shed bodily attachments, perceived the excellence of piety, and adhered to it.
rows.anchor: أي العقول الصافية والأفهام النيرة الخالصة التي تجردت عن جميع العلائق الجسمانية فأبصرت جلالة التقوى فلزمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since accumulating wealth is objectionable only when it distracts from remembering God, trade for benefit from God is permitted during pilgrimage seasons and at other times; one should rely on God for that benefit.
rows.anchor: أي إفادة بالمتجر في مواسم الحج وغيرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Ibn Abbas's report that people feared trading at pilgrimage markets in the pre-Islamic season, so this verse permitted it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : ( كانت عكاظ ومجنة وذو المجاز أسواقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of ifāḍa is understood: at sunset the pilgrims set their mounts moving and the procession flowed through the valleys like water down a slope.
rows.anchor: أي دفعتم ركابكم عند غروب الشمس ففاضت في تلك الوهاد كما يفيض الماء المنساب في منحدر الشعاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of ifāḍa is a forceful, abundant push.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإفاضة الدفع بكثرة { من عرفات } الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arafat is the mountain where pilgrims stand at the supreme station without which the pilgrimage is not attained; its name evokes recognition after an indefinite mention.
rows.anchor: الجبل الذي وقفتم فيه بباب ربكم الموقف الأعظم الذي لا يدرك الحج إلا به من معنى التعرف لما تقدمته نكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in ʿArafāt marks a feminine plural, not feminine gender; it is not the feminine ending that would make the name diptote.
rows.anchor: وليست تاؤه للتأنيث فتمنعه الصرف بل هي علامة جمع المؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿArafāt is a name for the standing place; the author also connects the name Jamʿ for the destination to its being a gathering place.
rows.anchor: وهو علم على الموقف سمي بجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sacred Monument is Mount Quzaḥ; the command is to remember God there for His own sake in every form of remembrance.
rows.anchor: أي قريبا من { المشعر } أي المعلم ولما كان بالحرم , قال : { الحرام } وهو الجبل المسمى قزح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mashʿar derives from inward, subtle perception; Arafat signifies the world's passing away, while Muzdalifah's dawn and sun signify resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: وهو من الشعور وهو خفي الإدراك الباطن فالموقف الأول آية على نغوض الدنيا ومحوها وزوالها , والثاني دال بفجره وشمسه على البعث لمجازاة الخلائق بأعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ʿinda means near, indicating that all of Muzdalifah except Muhassir is a standing place because it is near the monument; standing at the monument itself is valid a fortiori.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بعند للإعلام بأن مزدلفة كلها موقف غير محسر فإنها كلها تقاربه , ويفهم ذلك صحة الوقوف عليه بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Then can mark chronological sequence or the order of narration; discourse may mention the more important instruction first, so an earlier event can be delayed in the wording.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : لما كان للخطاب ترتيب للأهم فالأهم كما كان للكيان ترتيب للأسبق فالأسبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their long persistence in error, the Hums are commanded to depart once they have completed the standing, abandoning the Quraysh custom of claiming distinction by departing from Muzdalifah.
rows.anchor: ثم أفيضوا أيها الحمس ! { من حيث أفاض الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people from whose place the Hums must depart are the majority, namely those who stood at Arafat; they go from there to Muzdalifah to spend the night.
rows.anchor: أي معظمهم وهو عرفات , إلى المشعر الحرام لتبيتوا به

words: ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Aisha's report that Quraysh and their allies, the Hums, stood at Muzdalifah while other Arabs stood at Arafat; Islam ordered the Prophet to stand at Arafat and depart from it, as this verse states.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : ( كانت قريش ومن دان دينها يقفون بالمزدلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to seek forgiveness for their pre-Islamic departure from proper guidance, the lingering effects of that custom, and their other shortcomings known to God.
rows.anchor: أن يغفر لكم ما كنتم تفعلونه أيام جاهليتكم من مخالفة الهدى في الوقوف وما يبقى في الأنفس من آثار تلك العادة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali says inherited habits are among the hardest obstacles for worshippers; the path to God requires shedding them, and their uninformed argument for standing inside the sanctuary misconceived where fearful pilgrims should stand.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والعادات أشد ما على المتعبدين والطريق إلى الله تعالى بخلعها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali reasons that a person standing is fearful, whereas God made the sanctuary safe; therefore the proper standing is outside it, followed by entering the sanctuary in safety.
rows.anchor: فمن حق الوقوف أن يكون في الحل فإذا أمن دخل الحرم وإذا دخل الحرم أمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states God's name openly to present His attributes universally, without limiting them to a particular condition or perspective.
rows.anchor: وأظهر الاسم الشريف تعريفا للمقام وإعلاما بأنه موصوف بما يصفه به على وجه العموم من غير نظر إلى قيد ولا حيثية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafūr means that God conceals the sin of the person who seeks His forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أي ستور ذنب من استغفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's abundant mercy treats the repentant person as one who had no sin, welcoming them among the recipients of mercy.
rows.anchor: ليكون التائب من الذنب كمن لا ذنب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people tend to relax and stop remembering after completing worship, and Arabs then recited their ancestors' boasts, the command redirects remembrance to God after the rites.
rows.anchor: ولما أمرهم بالذكر في المناسك وكان الإنسان فيها بصدد الذكر أمرهم بالذكر بعد قضائها لأن من فرغ من العبادة كان بصدد أن يستريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though parents raised them, that upbringing ultimately comes from God; parents also exposed them to trials and misled them, while God is the ultimate source of their blessings and guidance.
rows.anchor: لكونهم أحسنوا إليكم بالتربية التي هي في الحقيقة من فضل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The change from the familiar formula of speech accompanies the change from the familiar pilgrimage station, breaking people of their accustomed practices and states.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : فانتظم ذكر إخراجهم عن قولهم المعهود بإخراجهم عن موقفهم المعهود

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali warns that people may treat God like an honored human because they are attached to what they see and have weak faith in what they hear or know.
rows.anchor: وذلك عن بلية ما غلب عليهم من التقيد بما يرون وضعف الإيمان بما سمعوا أو علموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the saying, Be ashamed before God as you would be ashamed before a dignified man among your people, as an analogy for the commanded reverence.
rows.anchor: استحي من الله كما تستحيي رجلا جليلا من قومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember God even more intensely because His beneficence is universal; shun associating a partner with Him at least as strongly as a son would reject a partner for his father.
rows.anchor: أي اذكروا الله ذكرا أعلى من ذلك بأن تذكروه ذكرا أشد من ذكركم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali says the command raises the discourse to what is more fitting for God: preferring what pertains to Him over what pertains to creatures.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : فرفع الخطاب إلى ما هو أ ليق بالحق من إيثار ما يرجع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding remembrance and exclusive devotion to God, the verse divides people according to whether they accept that command.
rows.anchor: سبب عنه تقسيم الناس في قبول الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first group has the world as its chief concern and asks only for worldly benefit, with no afterlife share because its members neither desire nor strive for it.
rows.anchor: تكون الدنيا أكبر همه فلا التفات له إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun with man follows the word's singular grammatical form; the author takes this as glad tidings that few in this community will be lost.
rows.anchor: أفرد الضمير رعاية للفظ من بشارة بأن الهالك في هذه الأمة إن شاء الله قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis leaves the object of the worldly request unstated, meaning whatever the supplicant wants.
rows.anchor: ومفعوله محذوف تقديره : ما نريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the expression may coordinate with an implied clause meaning God gives whatever He chooses, not necessarily what the supplicant requested.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون عطفا على ما تقديره : فيعطيه ما شاء سبحانه منها لا ما طلب هو

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali defines khalaq as a share suited to a person's created nature and character.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : والخلاق الحظ اللائق بالخلق والخلق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali explains worldly good as sufficient food, drink, clothing, shelter, and a spouse, without extravagance.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهي الكفاف من المطعم والمشرب والملبس والمأوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good of the afterlife is God's mercy by which He admits the supplicants to Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي من رحمتك التي تدخلنا بها الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplicant asks God to protect them from the Fire through His pardon and forgiveness, since hope must be accompanied by fear and worldly good does not rule out punishment.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الرجاء لا يصلح إلا بالخوف وإعطاء الحسنة لا ينفي المس بالسيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who pray this way follow the prophets: worship first, become humble, then remember God through three levels that illuminate the heart and prepare it for complete supplication, as Abraham did.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هؤلاء على منهاج الرسل لأنهم عبدوا الله أولا كما أشار إليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After identifying those destined for the Fire, the passage turns to people fit to hope for Paradise, so servants flee the causes of Hell and seek grounds for hope.
rows.anchor: ولما بين سبحانه وتعالى المقطوع لهم بالنار بين الذين هم أهل لرجاء الجنة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali summarizes the transition as moving from mention of the wavering to mention of the steadfast.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : لما ذكر أمر المتزلزلين ذكر أمر الثابتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here believing means affirming faith.
rows.anchor: فقال : { إن الذين آمنوا } أي أقروا بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun is repeated for migration and striving to mark their intrinsic importance: after leaving the homeland of religion, these are the hardest sacrifices for the self.
rows.anchor: كرر لهما الموصول إشعارا باستحقاقهما للاصالة في أنفسهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migration means leaving homes and people who oppose one's faith, including family and loved ones, out of aversion to them and in confirmation of one's professed belief.
rows.anchor: فارقوا بغضا ونفرة تصديقا لإقرارهم بذلك ديارهم ومن خالفهم فيه من أهلهم وأحبابهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali derives migration from abandoning something one would ordinarily cherish because it has become harmful.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من المهاجرة وهو مفاعلة من الهجرة وهو التخلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harali derives striving from exertion, whether the root is vocalized with fatḥa or ḍamma, and describes it as expending one's capacity through hardship in action.
rows.anchor: مفاعلة من الجهد - فتحا وضما , وهو الإبلاغ في الطاقة والمشقة في العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path of God means the religion of the supreme King, and those opposed to it are the adversaries against whom the believers strive.
rows.anchor: أي دين الملك الأعظم كل من خالفهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali defines hope as anticipating an outcome for which a cause has already been provided.
rows.anchor: من الرجاء وهو ترقب الانتفاء بما تقدم له سبب ما - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers hope but do not claim certainty, since God may do as He wills and they cannot be sure they will die in a state of virtue.
rows.anchor: غير قاطعين بذلك علما منهم أن له أن يفعل ما يشاء لأنه الملك الأعظم فلا كفوء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hope is joined to fear: if God were to judge them for the sins He knows, He could punish them.
rows.anchor: قاطعون بأنه سبحانه وتعالى لو أخذهم بما يعلم من ذنوبهم عذبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving by concealing minor sins or major sins for which people have repented.
rows.anchor: أي ستور لما فرط منهم من الصغائر أو تابوا عنه من الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy means treating them with beneficence, honor, and a welcoming reception of divine approval.
rows.anchor: فاعل بهم فعل الراحم من الإحسان والإكرام والاستقبال بالرضى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali reads the repeated endings with mercy as a sign that God's favor in this life and the next is grace given at the outset, not payment truly earned by deeds.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي الختم بالرحمة أبدا في خواتم الآي إشعار بأن فضل الله في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine was then allowed during the night of fasting; people commonly drank date and raisin nabīdh, which could ferment in the hot climate.
rows.anchor: كان الشراب مما أذن فيه في ليل الصيام وكان غالب شرابهم النبيذ من التمر والزبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intoxication obstructs worship, especially military striving, because a drunk person cannot contribute judgment or physical force.
rows.anchor: فكان عائقا عن العبادة لا سيما الجهاد لأن السكران لا ينتفع به في رأي ولا بطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike food, wine was not necessary to sustain the body, so explaining its status could be deferred until more urgent matters were addressed.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن ضروريا في إقامة البدن كالطعام آخر بيانه إلى أن فرغ مما هو أولى منه بالإعلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the intervening verses were concluded by returning to the theme of striving with which they began, before later verses on permissions.
rows.anchor: وختم الآيات المتخللة بينه وبين آيات الإذن بما بدأها به من الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing striving as a ground for hoping in mercy, the passage fittingly turns to what the author calls the greatest folly and sources of evils: wine and gambling.
rows.anchor: الجهاد وما ذكر معه في محل الرجاء للرحمة فاقتضى الحال السؤال : هل سالوا عن أهزل الهزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says wine was among the spoils taken by Abdullah ibn Jahsh's expedition, which occasioned the preceding verses.
rows.anchor: أحد ما غنمه عبد الله بن جحش رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali relates khamr to covering: vegetation hides what is visible, while wine conceals the intellect and obscures the boundary between clear reason and brute animality.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو مما منه الخمر - بفتح الميم - وهو ما وارى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali defines wine as anything intoxicating, whatever the drink and whether its amount is small or large.
rows.anchor: وهي ما أسكر من اي شراب كان سواء فيه القليل والكثير

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali calls maysir a pre-Islamic gambling institution intended to benefit the weak and to gain the spoils of victory.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : اسم مقامرة كانت الجاهلية تعمل بها لقصد انتفاع الضعفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine and gambling are paired because both undermine striving and other goods by transferring wealth without the owner's willing consent.
rows.anchor: لتآخيهما في الضرر بالجهاد وغيره بإذهاب المال مجانا عن غير طيب نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says wine and gambling are paired here as they are in the Maidah passage.
rows.anchor: ما بين سبحانه وتعالى من المؤاخاة بينهما هنا وفي المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to using or consuming both wine and gambling.
rows.anchor: { قل فيهما } أي في استعمالهما { إثم كبير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sin includes lying, abuse, loss of reason, and taking another's property; declaring the acts sinful establishes their prohibition and identifies them as major sins.
rows.anchor: لما فيهما من المساوي المنابذة لمحاسن الشرع من الكذب والشتم وزوال العقل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Harali notes readings with bāʾ and thāʾ, كبير and كثير, which indicate both great magnitude and large quantity of sin; either should deter a sound person.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : في قراءتي الباء الموحدة والمثلثة إنباء عن مجموع الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author frames the question and gradual explanation as an expression of divine forbearance, leaving matters beyond the subject at pure permissibility.
rows.anchor: مبينا لما اقتضاه الحال من حلمه فيبقى ما عداه على الإباحة المحضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The benefits people seek include trading in wine, enjoying its taste, winning money through gambling, aiding the poor, boasting over nonparticipants, and gaining companions and their food, drink, and gifts.
rows.anchor: يرتكبونهما لأجلها من التجارة في الخمر واللذة بشربها , ومن أخذ المال الكثير في الميسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sin outweighs the benefits, the harms take precedence; the author invokes the principle that preventing harms comes first.
rows.anchor: ودرء المفاسد مقدم فكيف { وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما }

rows.speaker: أهل المعرفة
rows.claim: Some people of insight said the benefit of gambling was that, during winter and famine, Arabs wagered camels and gave the meat to the poor, improving their circumstances.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعرفة : والنفع الذي ذكر الله في الميسر أن العرب في الشتاء والجدب

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: The author cites al-Aʿsha's line praising people who feed guests in winter and distribute provisions through the gambling shares as evidence for the reported benefit.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى في ذلك : المطعمو الضيف إذا ما شتوا والجاعلو القوت على الياسر

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another account says gamblers gave the meat to the poor without eating it themselves, boasted of the generosity, and called a person who abstained al-barm.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره : وكانوا يدفعونها للفقراء ولا يأكلون منها ويفتخرون بذلك

rows.speaker: المجد الفيروزآبادي
rows.claim: Al-Fayruzabadi's dictionary defines maysir as playing with arrows, the camel staked in the game, backgammon, or gambling in general.
rows.anchor: قال المجد الفيروز آبادي في قاموسه : والميسر اللعب بالقداح

rows.speaker: صاحب كتاب الزينة
rows.claim: The lexicon gives yusr as the plural of yāsir and aysār as the plural of yusr, illustrating a plural formed from another plural.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب كتاب الزينة : وجمع الياسر يسر وجمع اليسر أيسار فهو جمع الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qimār is any wager based purely on uncertain risk; the author derives its name from the moon because a gambler's wealth waxes and wanes like the moon.
rows.anchor: والقمار كل مراهنة على غرر محض وكأنه مأخوذ من القمر آية الليل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid is quoted as defining maysir broadly as anything involving gambling, even children playing with walnuts.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : كل شيء فيه قمار فهو الميسر حتى لعب الصبيان بالجوز

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is quoted as defining maysir as any game requiring a person to pay or receive money; chess without a wager, abusive speech, or missed prayer is not maysir.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الأصبهاني عن الشافعي : إن الميسر ما يوجب دفع مال أو أخذ مال

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari derives maysir from dividing the staked camel into shares; yāsir first meant the butcher who apportioned its meat, then the gamblers who caused the slaughter.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري : الميسر الجزور الذي كانوا يتقامرون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing al-Azhari's lexical entry, the text records yasar al-qawm for gambling and yāsir or yusr for a gambler, with aysār as the plural.
rows.anchor: يسر القوم - إذا قامروا

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz gives forms for the person who gambles and the camel staked in the game, and records aysāʾ as a plural of yusr.
rows.anchor: القزاز : فأنت ياسر وهو ميسور برجع والمفعول ميسور - يعني الجزور

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz calls the gamblers collectively yusr, with an individual yāsir; he also uses yusr for an arrow thrower and maysir for dice, but not chess because its meaning differs.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز : واليسر القوم الذين يتقامرون على الجزور

rows.speaker: عبد الحق
rows.claim: Abd al-Haqq defines maysir as the place where portions are divided.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الحق في الواعي : والميسر موضع التجزئة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah describes buying and slaughtering a camel, then dividing it into portions.
rows.anchor: أبو عبد الله : كان أمر الميسر أنهم كانوا يشترون جزورا فينحرونها ثم يجزئونها أجزاء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والأصمعي
rows.claim: Abu Amr says the camel was divided into ten portions, while al-Asmaʿi says there were twenty-eight.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو : على عشرة أجزاء , وقال الأصمعي : على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ten arrows were drawn: seven carried shares and three were blank; a trusted, impartial man drew an arrow for each participant, and winners received shares according to the arrow.
rows.anchor: ثم يسهمون عليها بعشرة قداح , لسبعة منها أنصباء وهي الفذ

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported view says a person drawing a blank arrow neither wins nor pays; the drawing is repeated, and that person's turn is treated as void.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : من خرجت باسمه لم يأخذ شيئا ولم يغرم ولكن تعاد الثانية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A competing view says the holders of the three blank arrows pay the entire camel's price, while the seven winning holders take their allotted shares.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل يصير ثمن الجزور كله على أصحاب هؤلاء الثلاثة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd says scholars did not fully explain the game; Abu Ubayda asked Bedouins, who no longer knew its rules because Islam had ended it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد : ولم أجد علماءنا يستقصون علم معرفة هذا ولا يدعونه

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says the Bedouins he asked did not know the game, which Islam had ended, so they could not explain its rules.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : وقد سألت عنه الأعراب فقالوا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd says the game was practiced among people of high status, wealth, and means.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد : وإنما كان هذا منهم في أهل الشرف والثروة والجدة

rows.speaker: صاحب الزينة
rows.claim: The Zina account calls arrows that carry a share marked because their shares are assigned; seven people each held one arrow, though a player might hold two and be praised for it.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الزينة : فالتي لها الغنم وعليها الغرم أي من السهام

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse praises giving people two shares each and clothing a group, cited in connection with a player taking two arrows.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة : إني أتمم إيثاري وأمنحهم مثنى الأيادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ḥarḍa draws the arrows but does not participate or share in winnings or losses, so gamblers choose him; al-barm is the person who declines to participate.
rows.anchor: ويقال للذي يضرب بالقداح : حرضة , وإنما سمي بذلك لأنه رجل يجيل لا يدخل مع الأيسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-barm is someone who neither draws arrows nor joins the gamblers in any of their affairs.
rows.anchor: والذي لا يضرب القداح ولا يدخل مع الأيسار في شيء من أمورهم يقال له : البرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrow pouch is called ribāba; it could be leather or cloth, and its ends were gathered and leveled before the draw.
rows.anchor: وتجمع القداح في جلدة , وقال بعضهم : في خرقة , وتسمى تلك الجلدة الربابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To prevent choosing an arrow by touch, the drawer's hand was covered in leather and his eyes bound; he gathered the arrows and struck their tips so one emerged as the winner.
rows.anchor: وتكسى يده أديما لكي لا يجد مس قدح له فيه رأي وتشد عيناه , فيجمع أصابعه عليها

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another account says the winning arrow was the one that emerged from the pouch without being deflected or obstructed.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره : تكون الربابة فلا يخرج ومنها ما لا يعترض فيطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trusted person beside the ḥarḍa was called raqīb, and the arrow drawer mufīḍ; ifāḍa means pushing the arrows forward together.
rows.anchor: ويقعد رجل أمين على الحرضة يقال له : الرقيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author connects the arrow drawer's ifāḍa with pilgrimage ifāḍa, the push from Arafat to Jamʿ.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الإفاضة من عرفة هو الدفع منها إلى جمع

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus says gamblers bought a camel on credit, slaughtered it, and divided it into 28 shares or ten portions; the winning arrows took shares while blank arrows incurred the cost.
rows.anchor: وقال في القاموس : كانوا إذا أرادوا أن ييسروا اشتروا جزورا نسيئة

rows.speaker: عبد الغافر الفارسي
rows.claim: Abd al-Ghafir al-Farsi describes maysir as pre-Islamic gambling over a camel or other property divided into shares, but notes that accounts differ and Muslim lexicographers lacked firm knowledge of its procedure.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الغافر الفارسي في مجمع الغرائب : الياسر هو الضارب في القداح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To aid memorization, the author lists seven winning arrows and three blank ones: al-fadh, al-taw'am, al-raqib, al-hils, al-nafis, al-musbil, al-muʿalla, al-maniḥ, al-safih, and al-waghd.
rows.anchor: وقد نظمت أسماء القداح تسهيلا لحفظها في قولي : الفذ والتوأم والرقيب

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines al-fadh as the first arrow of maysir and begins its definitions of the taw'am and raqib arrows.
rows.anchor: فقال في القاموس : الفذ أي بفتح الفاء وتشديد الذال المعجمة : أول سهام الميسر

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines ḍarīb as the person who oversees or draws the arrows, and also as the third arrow.
rows.anchor: وقال في مادة ضرب : والضريب الموكل بالقداح أو الذي يضرب بها

rows.speaker: صاحب الجمع بين العباب والمحكم
rows.claim: The dictionary collection defines raqīb as a keeper or custodian of the arrows, an umpire near the ḥarḍa, or the third arrow, all related uses of the same term.
rows.anchor: وقال في الجمع بين العباب والمحكم : والرقيب الحافظ ورقيب القداح الأمين على الضريب

rows.speaker: صاحب الجمع بين العباب والمحكم
rows.claim: The third raqib arrow carries three shares: its holder wins three shares or owes three if it loses.
rows.anchor: والرقيب الثالث من قداح الميسر , وفيه ثلاثة فروض , وله غنم ثلاثة انصباء إن فاز

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says ḍarīb has the faʿīl form with the active-agent sense; ḍarīb also names the third arrow, called al-raqib.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه : فعيل بمعنى فاعل

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines ḥarḍa as the game steward, al-ḥils as the fourth arrow, al-nafis as fifth, and al-musbil as sixth or fifth.
rows.anchor: وقال في القاموس : والحرضة أي بضم المهملة وإسكان المهملة ثم معجمة أمين المقامرين

rows.speaker: مجمع البحرين
rows.claim: Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn gives al-muṣaffah as another name for al-musbil.
rows.anchor: وقال في مجمع البحرين : وهو المصفح أيضا يعني بفتح الفاء

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus calls al-muʿalla the seventh arrow and defines al-maniḥ and al-safih as blanks; al-waghd is both a blank arrow and a fool, weakling, or contemptible person.
rows.anchor: والمعلى كمعظم سابع سهام الميسر , والمنيح كأمير أي بنون وآخره مهملة قدح بلا نصيب

rows.speaker: صاحب الزينة
rows.claim: The Zina account says the camel was divided into ten shares; al-raqib could draw repeatedly, taking three shares each time, and when the camel was exhausted the remaining players paid according to their shares.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الزينة : وكانوا يبتاعون الجزور ويتضمنون ثمنه ثم يضربون بالقداح عليه

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi instead assigns 28 shares to the arrows, beginning with one for al-fadh and two for al-taw'am; the author reports that most scholars disagreed and considered him mistaken.
rows.anchor: وذكر عن الأصمعي أنه قال : كانوا يقسمون الجزور على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا
